jokes: In ROS 2 your publisher and subscriber can both be alive, healthy, and perfectly configured, and still never speak to each other. Just like my parents.
sqlite3 bags: where your messages wait in a relational table, wondering why mcap got the promotion and they didn't. Relatable.
Python venvs in ROS: you can create one, activate one, and believe in one. You just can't actually have one. Faith-based isolation.

I spent a day tuning my QoS profile: reliable, transient_local, keep_last, depth tuned to perfection. The subscriber used the defaults. They never matched, never spoke, and never told me why. Classic.
I set my QoS to best_effort, which in ROS 2 means 'the message might arrive.' Honestly the most accurate description of any effort I've ever made.
colcon told me 'Failed   <<< my_package' and nothing else. Not why, not where, not how. Just that it failed, and that I should already know. We were raised the same way.
To see what's in one rosbag I open three terminals: one to play it, one to echo it, one to wonder where my life went. The data shows up eventually. The meaning never does.
ROS stands for Robot Operating System, except it isn't an operating system. It's middleware wearing the name of something more important than it is. We have that in common.
ROS: a Robot Operating System that doesn't manage memory, schedule processes, or boot a machine. It manages topics and an identity crisis. Relatable, frankly.
ros2 bag play gives a different result every run, depending on CPU load, scheduling, and how the machine feels that morning. My simulation isn't deterministic; it's moody. We get along.
ros2 bag play: the only simulation where the result depends on whether you also had Slack open. Science.
ROS custom messages: choose your fields carefully, because that .msg is forever. It's not a schema, it's a tattoo.

dora-rs moves data in microseconds with zero-copy Rust. I'm still shaking hands over DDS, asking if the subscriber's there yet. But I have a decade of packages for every sensor ever made... so you won't abandon me, right? You'll keep using me?
